Q: Thank you for taking the time to speak with me today. This recorded statement concerns the collision you were
involved in. Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather not give my full name on a recording, but you already have it on the claim file.
Q: That's fine. For the record, we'll reference the claim file. Can you walk me through where you were when the
collision happened?
A: I was in League City, heading toward a shopping center on the left side of the road. I had my turn signal on and
was waiting for a gap in oncoming traffic.
Q: What happened next?
A: A vehicle coming from the opposite direction came through while I was already partway into the turn. It hit the front
passenger side of my car. I didn't see it until it was too late.
Q: Was your vehicle movnig when the impact happened, or had you stopped?
A: I was moving slowly, maybe ten or fifteen miles an hour, still committed to the turn.
Q: Did you notice any injuries right away?
A: Not immediately. My neck started stiffening within an hour or so, and by that evening my lower back was sore and
tight. I've been stretching and using a heating pad. It's been hard to sit for long periods.
Q: Have you sought any medical treatment?
A: Yes, I was seen at an urgent care clinic the next day. They diagnosed me with a neck strain and a lower back
strain and told me to rest and follow up with my primary doctor.
Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add?
A: Just that I was trying to drive carefully, and I'm hoping the other driver's insurer will take responsibility for the
damage. I'm willing to provide any records you need.
Q: Thank you. This concludes the recorded statement.
</page>
